label: ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini
text: The deck opens with the people behind three AI tools, shown with the ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini logos.

label: Haptik
text: Enterprise conversational AI platform (text and voice chatbots) used in insurance, e-commerce and government; the MyGov Corona Helpdesk reached 30M+ users.

label: Yellow.ai
text: Omnichannel customer support automation platform; also launched YellowG, a small generative AI model.

label: Krutrim (Kruti)
text: Kruti, India's first agentic AI assistant: books taxis, orders food, pays bills; supports 13 Indian languages.

label: Sarvam AI
text: Language-specific LLMs for 10 Indian languages, voice-enabled chatbots, and the open-source 2B-parameter model Sarvam 2B.

label: Lumio AI
text: A multi-model AI platform that lets users compare and switch between ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and more via a single interface.

label: CoRover.ai (BharatGPT)
text: BharatGPT, a sovereign AI assistant offering text, voice and video outputs tailored for India.

label: Zoho Corporation
text: In-house LLM and AI agents integrated across its productivity suite for drafting, analysis and automation.

label: Hey Siri
text: A phone showing Hey Siri illustrates AI that simulates human behaviour.

label: AI market size
text: The global AI market: USD 86.9 billion in 2022, projected USD 407.0 billion by 2027, a CAGR of 36.2%.

label: Narrow AI examples
text: Netflix, Siri, Alexa and Face ID as examples of task-specific narrow AI.

label: General AI examples
text: ChatGPT, IBM Watson and Google Gemini listed as examples of general AI that learns across domains.

label: AI, ML and DL examples
text: AI: chatbots, facial recognition, recommendation engines. ML: spam email filtering, stock prediction, language translation. DL: voice assistants, image classification, autonomous driving.

label: AI in marketing examples
text: Jasper AI and ChatGPT creating Instagram captions; Haptik or Drift answering FAQs; Mailchimp sending birthday offers; forecasting sales spikes before Diwali; Google Ads auto-bidding; Meta (Facebook) suggesting products.

label: AI tutors in training
text: Employee training uses AI tutors and adaptive learning platforms such as Coursera and LinkedIn Learning.

label: Companies using AI in Industry 4.0
text: GE, Siemens, Bosch and Caterpillar (predictive maintenance); IBM Watson (sensor data, equipment failures); Tesla (quality checks, assembly lines); Amazon (demand, inventory, delivery routes); ABB (ML in robotics); John Deere (precision agriculture); P&G (supply chain and manufacturing).

label: Employers for AI-literate MBAs
text: Deloitte, McKinsey, EY, BCG and Accenture for AI strategy consulting; Goldman Sachs, Paytm, Razorpay and ICICI for AI-powered finance roles.

label: Professions at risk
text: Data entry clerks, customer service agents, bank tellers, telemarketers, basic bookkeepers, paralegals, media content writers, travel agents, proofreaders and entry-level coders, each with the AI capability replacing it.

label: AI tool wipes a database
text: A news video: AI Assistant Tool Wipes Out Entire Company Database (GRAVITAS).

label: AI demand in business schools and hiring
text: Over 75% of business schools weave AI into their curricula; 74% of employers look for AI/ML proficiency in MBA grads, lifting AI from 21st to 4th among sought-after competencies (e-GMAT); 66% of organizational leaders won't hire candidates lacking AI literacy (Microsoft CDN).

label: Schools embedding AI
text: Leading schools like Wharton, Kogod, Columbia, Duke, Stanford and Harvard actively embed AI tools into core subjects.

label: Student AI usage
text: 82% of students use AI weekly and 39% daily (Microsoft CDN, DataCamp).

label: Datathons with Bloomberg and Amazon
text: Schools report AI-enabled projects, workshops and hackathons, e.g. datathons with Bloomberg, Amazon, to boost hands-on experience (Study International).

label: UK study on institutional support
text: A UK study shows only 36% of students receive institutional support in 2025: formal training remains inconsistent.

label: Intermediate-level AI projects
text: Projects at the intermediate level: AI for crop disease, traffic prediction, sentiment analysis.

label: Applications at scale (advanced level)
text: Real-world applications with scale: chatbots, recommendation engines, autonomous systems.

label: John McCarthy
text: John McCarthy, who coined the term AI in 1956, defined it as "The science and engineering of making intelligent machines."

label: Russell and Norvig
text: Modern view by experts like Russell and Norvig: "AI is the study of agents that perceive their environment and take actions that maximize their chances of achieving their goals."

label: Arthur Samuel's checkers program
text: 1959: Arthur Samuel creates one of the first machine learning programs (checkers).

label: Alan Turing
text: In 1950 Alan Turing published his landmark paper "Computing Machinery and Intelligence" and, instead of asking "Can machines think?", proposed the Turing Test.

label: Logic Theorist
text: Developed in 1956 by Allen Newell & Herbert A. Simon at RAND Corporation; proved 38 mathematical theorems from Principia Mathematica and is considered the first AI program.

label: ELIZA
text: 1966, created at MIT by Joseph Weizenbaum; simulated a psychotherapist by asking reflective questions, using simple keyword pattern matching. The first successful chatbot.

label: PARRY
text: 1972, developed by Kenneth Colby to simulate a patient with paranoid schizophrenia; unlike ELIZA it had internal beliefs and emotional states.

label: Catherine
text: 1991, the next generation of conversational systems: larger knowledge bases, improved dialogue management, more natural conversations.

label: Eugene Goostman
text: 2000, a chatbot designed as a 13-year-old Ukrainian boy; in 2014 some reports claimed it passed the Turing Test, which remains debated.

label: Cleverbot
text: 2011, learned from millions of previous conversations and predicts the most likely response: a shift from rule-based to data-driven AI.

label: XCON
text: An expert system at Digital Equipment Corp, the slide's example of the 1980s rise of expert systems.

label: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
text: 1997: IBM's Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov, showing the power of AI in complex strategic reasoning.

label: AlexNet
text: AlexNet (2012) won the ImageNet competition with 85% accuracy, 10% better than anyone before, using deep CNNs + ReLU activation + dropout + two GPUs.

label: AlphaGo
text: 2016: AlphaGo defeats the Go champion, using deep reinforcement learning combined with tree search.

label: IndiaAI Mission
text: India launches the IndiaAI Mission (2024) with a ₹10,300 Cr investment.

label: Lighthill Report
text: DARPA and the UK's Lighthill Report (1973) criticized AI's limited results and halted major funding, part of the 1st AI Winter.

label: Japan's 5th Generation Project
text: Japan's 5th Generation Project fell short of revolutionizing computing, damaging global AI momentum, part of the 2nd AI Winter.

label: MapReduce and AWS
text: Google's Jeff Dean & Sanjay Ghemawat built MapReduce and the Google File System to process massive datasets; Amazon Web Services (AWS) made storage and distributed computing affordable.

label: CUDA
text: CUDA (Compute Unified Device Architecture), developed by Ian Buck at NVIDIA in 2006, let researchers write general-purpose programs on GPUs.

label: Godfathers of Deep Learning
text: Geoffrey Hinton, Yann LeCun and Yoshua Bengio, known as the Godfathers of Deep Learning, won the Turing Award in 2018.

label: AI market by phase
text: About $8 billion industry by mid-2000s; AI market ~$279 b in 2024, projected to $1.8 t by 2030; DL market $125 b in 2025; DL market ~93 b (2024) to ~$1.42 t (2034).

label: Products of the AI Renaissance
text: The AI Renaissance, launched around 2012, laid the foundation for GPT, DALL·E, AlphaFold, ChatGPT and many more.

label: IBM Watson on Jeopardy!
text: IBM Watson was built to compete on the US quiz show Jeopardy! and in 2011 defeated top human champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter. It used the DeepQA architecture and was later applied in healthcare (cancer diagnosis), finance (risk management) and legal services.

label: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
text: AlphaGo, created by DeepMind (a Google subsidiary), defeated world champion Lee Sedol at the board game Go in 2016, using deep neural networks, reinforcement learning and Monte Carlo Tree Search.

label: GPT-1 to GPT-4
text: GPT-1 (2018) proof of concept; GPT-2 (2019) first widely capable model, initially withheld over safety concerns; GPT-3 (2020) 175B parameters; GPT-4 (2023) multimodal. GPTs power ChatGPT, Copilot (coding), DALL·E (images) and Whisper (speech).

label: Narrow AI examples
text: Netflix recommendation system (suggests shows from viewing history); face recognition apps (Face ID, Aadhaar authentication, security surveillance); Google Maps, Siri and Alexa (navigation, reminders); spam filters (block junk emails).

label: General AI examples
text: OpenAI GPT-4 / GPT-3 / Gemini (research, tutoring, problem-solving, coding); IBM Watson (hospitals and enterprises: medical records, logistics); AI writing assistants such as Grammarly or Copilot.

label: Imagined uses of super AI
text: Robots that replace doctors, teachers and judges; AI that solves climate change or space colonization; fully autonomous societies run by AI, as in the sci-fi movies Her or Ex Machina.

label: Popular ANI systems
text: ChatGPT (OpenAI) for conversation, summarization, Q&A and code; Google Bard / Gemini for conversational AI; Siri / Alexa / Google Assistant and Descript / Otter.ai for speech; Netflix, Spotify and Amazon for recommendations; IBM Watson for medical diagnosis, legal reasoning and enterprise decisions; Waymo (by Alphabet) for self-driving; PathAI for AI-based pathology diagnosis.

label: ANI market by domain
text: Combined ANI market USD 230 to 280 billion (2024) to USD 1.8 trillion by 2030; enterprise / predictive analytics USD 24 billion (2024) to USD 155 billion by 2030 at about 37.6%; AI agents / conversational bots USD 5.25 billion (2024) to USD 52.6 billion by 2030; big data + AI USD 420 billion (2025 est.) to USD 1.54 trillion by 2034 at about 15.6%.

label: India's AI market
text: India's AI market was around USD 8 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 17 billion by 2027 at an annual growth rate of 25 to 40%, driven by enterprise deployments, government initiatives and AI talent growth.

label: Modern technologies are adopted faster
text: It took five decades for U.S. households to go from 10% adoption of electricity to 99%; it took just 15 years for social media to go from 5% adoption to 79%.

label: ChatGPT weekly active users
text: ChatGPT weekly active users grew from 100 million (Nov 2023) to 200 million (Aug 2024), 300 million (Dec 2024), 400 million (Feb 2025) and 800 million (Mar 2025).

label: Hey Siri, what's the weather?
text: Voice input "Hey Siri, what's weather today?" goes through speech recognition, natural language processing and query resolution to the response "It's currently 72°F and sunny."

label: Siri vs Alexa vs Google Assistant
text: Siri 87 million users (integrated with devices, focus on privacy); Alexa 76 million users (high device penetration, significant losses); Google Assistant 82 million users (bundled with products, advertising revenue).

label: Use cases of ANI
text: General AI market (cross-domain ANI's): GPT-4, Gemini, Claude, IBM Watson. Marketing & text AI: Grammarly, ChatGPT, Jasper AI, Google Translate. Enterprise & predictive analytics AI: IBM Watson, Salesforce Einstein, Zest AI. AI agents / chatbots: Alexa, Siri, Google Assistant, Intercom, Drift. Big data + AI platforms: Azure ML, AWS SageMaker, Google Vertex AI.

label: ANI in business: retail, healthcare, BFSI
text: Retail: recommendation engines, dynamic pricing, inventory management (personalized experiences, rapid market growth). Healthcare: diagnostic image analysis, predictive risk modeling, fraud detection (improved accuracy, $29 billion in 2024). BFSI: fraud detection, credit scoring, AI chatbots (faster service response, $26.2 billion in 2024).

label: Case studies of AGI definitions
text: Turing Test (too reliant on deception); Strong AI, Searle (requires consciousness); brain analogy (not necessary for performance); cognitive tasks, Legg and Goertzel (capability, not embodiment); learning tasks, Shanahan (metacognitive ability); economic value, OpenAI (excludes non-economic intelligence); real-world tasks, Marcus and Suleyman (flexibility and generality); LLMs as AGI, Arcas and Norvig (generality present, performance lacking).

label: Levels of AGI
text: Level 0: No AI (calculators); Level 1: Emerging AGI (ChatGPT); Level 2: Competent AGI (not yet achieved); Level 3: Expert AGI; Level 4: Virtuoso AGI; Level 5: ASI.

label: Levels of autonomy
text: Tool (basic automation, e.g. grammar checker), Consultant (advice when prompted), Collaborator (shared goals), Expert (AI leads, human gives feedback), Agent (fully autonomous AI).

label: Timeline of AI technologies (Figure 3)
text: Early AI: 1950s; Narrow AI: 2010s; AGI: predicted for mid-21st century; ASI: hypothetical future; UBI: Universal Basic Intelligence, future concept.

label: AI applications by business function (Figure 4)
text: Marketing 30%, Customer Service 20%, Supply Chain Management 15%, Research and Development 15%, Finance and Accounting 10%, Human Resources 10%.

label: Task-technology fit matrix (Figure 6)
text: Fit of ML, NLP, RPA, data analytics and anomaly detection with risk assessment, auditing, transaction monitoring, compliance checking and fraud detection, rated High, Medium or Low; the only Low is NLP for transaction monitoring.

label: Real-time activity-based costing
text: Real-time activity-based costing (ABC) optimizes operations, for example a 25% cost reduction in logistics.

label: Internal control case studies
text: Manufacturing company: AI in inventory control improved demand forecasting, 20% inventory reduction, proactive supplier monitoring. Financial institution: AI-based fraud detection cut losses by 30%, automated compliance improved regulatory response. Tech firm: AI analysed employee performance and project data, boosting productivity by 25%.

label: How AI keeps learning (Figure 14)
text: Initial Learning (2022), Continuous Learning (2023), Advanced Learning (2024), Mature Learning (2025): AI moves from basic models and small datasets to real-time autonomous decision-making.

label: Tesla driverless car
text: A labelled drawing: cameras (360-degree vision), AI chip (processing sensor data), GPS & IMU (localization), radar (forward-looking perception) and an ultrasonic sensor.

label: Thinkers behind ASI
text: Nick Bostrom (Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies); Ray Kurzweil (The Singularity is Near); Elon Musk and Stephen Hawking warned about uncontrolled ASI posing existential risks.

label: Global AI safety bodies
text: Institutions like the OECD, the UN and partnerships such as the Partnership on AI are working on global AI safety protocols.
